content.title: AKU becomes smoke-free
content.summary: The Aga Khan University is "smoke-free" from January 01, 2001. This is the first step towards the anti-smoking campaign being launched by the AKU.

content.text: The Aga Khan University is "smoke-free" from January 01, 2001. This is the first step towards the anti-smoking campaign being launched by the AKU.

The decision to declare its premises smoke-free was taken by Dr. Shamsh Kassim-Lakha, President, AKU, at the last World No Tobacco Day. In the past few months, AKU has taken several measures to educate its employees including doctors, nurses and allied health professionals on the harmful effects of tobacco, as well as to cut down the use of tobacco within the campus. The University has also started special clinics on smoking cessation for its employees. Tobacco use is on the rise in Pakistan and by declaring its premises smoke-free, AKU is trying to bring anti-smoking culture in the society, said Dr Javaid Khan, Chairman AKU 'Tobacco OR Health' Committee.

Dr Javaid Khan, a Consultant of Chest Diseases at AKUH, regretted that the aggressive advertising and promotional strategies by the tobacco companies are hooking millions of Pakistanis to this powerful addiction. The teenagers are the most vulnerable targets. Approximately 1,200 children in Pakistan take up smoking every day. Fifty-four per cent of men and 20 per cent of women in the country are addicted to tobacco, and this number is increasing every day. Studies in Pakistan have shown that almost 50 per cent of children get exposed to the dangers of the environmental tobacco smoke (ETS). There is a need to ban smoking at public places in order to protect children and non-smokers from the harmful effects of passive smoking. Scientific research has shown that long-term exposure to ETS increases the risk of dying from the disease by 30 per cent in non-smokers.

Dr Khan added that almost 40 per cent of all cancers and 95 per cent of lung cancers in Pakistan could be prevented if tobacco use is stopped. Besides cancer, tobacco is the most important risk factor for heart attacks, chronic bronchitis, strokes and gangrene.
